sources: Connecting Your GoDaddy Domain to Wix via Pointing
Connecting a Domain to the Wix Name Servers
Connecting a Domain to Wix Using the Pointing Method
response:
You can connect a GoDaddy domain to your Wix site in two ways. Here's the GoDaddy pointing method, which keeps your DNS at GoDaddy:

**Before you begin:** Make sure your site is upgraded with a plan and your domain is added to your Wix account (Domains in your Wix account > Add an Existing Domain > Connect a domain you already own).

**Steps in GoDaddy:**
1. Sign in to your GoDaddy account.
2. Click the user profile icon at the top right and select **My Products**.
3. Click **DNS** to the right of your domain.
4. Click the **Edit** icon next to the A record that has **@** in the Name column, and update it with the Wix records shown in your Wix dashboard.

Note that with pointing, Wix can't help manage your DNS, so GoDaddy support is the place for DNS questions. Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/connecting-your-godaddy-domain-to-wix-via-pointing-9528059

If you'd rather let Wix manage your DNS, you can instead connect via name servers. Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/connecting-a-domain-to-the-wix-name-servers

sources: Wix Stores Setting Up Free Shipping Above a Set Price
Wix Stores Creating Popular Store Discounts
Wix Stores Setting Up Free Shipping
response:
You can offer free shipping on orders over $50 in one of two ways:

**Option 1: Add it to a shipping rule**

1. Go to the **Shipping & fulfillment** settings in your site's dashboard.
2. Click **Edit Shipping Rule** and select a Flat Rate, Rate by Weight, or Rate by Product rule.
3. Select the **Offer free shipping on orders above a specific subtotal** checkbox.
4. Enter **50** as the price above which shipping is free.
5. Click **Save**.

If you offer additional shipping services (such as Express Shipping), select the checkbox and enter the amount for each one. You'll need to do this for every relevant shipping region.

**Option 2: Create a temporary free shipping coupon**

1. Click **+New Coupon** and select **Free Shipping**.
2. Enter a coupon code and coupon name.
3. Under **Apply to**, select **Minimum order subtotal** and enter **$50**.
4. Click **Create Coupon**.

The shipping rule option works as a permanent offer, while the coupon is useful for a temporary promotion.

response:
You can close your Wix account once it has no active services left. Here's the process:

1. **Cancel or transfer premium services.** Go to Premium Subscriptions and cancel each plan, domain, mailbox, or app. Alternatively, transfer a premium site or domain to another account. Canceling a Wix domain can take up to 80 days to fully clear.
2. **Remove external domains.** Go to Domains, click the Domain Actions icon next to the domain, and click Remove from Wix.
3. **Move your sites to Trash.** In each site's dashboard, click the Site Actions icon at the top, then click Move to Trash and confirm.
4. **Close your account.** Once everything above is done, click Close Account.

If you can't log in, reset your password first. Full details are in the [Closing Your Wix Account](https://support.wix.com/en/article/closing-your-wix-account) article.

Wix Bookings Refunding Clients
Wix Retail POS Accepting Exchanges from Customers
response:
A chargeback happens when a customer asks their bank or card provider to return their money. Unlike a regular refund, it involves the banks and payment networks too. Here's what to know:

- **Chargeback fee:** You're charged a fee when you receive a chargeback (15.00 in your local currency, e.g. USD, EUR or GBP). If you win the dispute, the fee and the payment amount are returned to you.
- **Your options:** You can either accept the chargeback, in which case the funds stay with your customer, or dispute it if you have evidence that the payment was valid.
- **Checking status:** Go to your Wix Payments dashboard and check the status next to the payment. Statuses include Action needed, Expires in X days, Disputed, Won, Lost, Accepted and Final.

**To dispute a chargeback:**

1. Go to Payments in your site's dashboard and click the payment.
2. Click Get Started, then Dispute Chargeback under the chargeback's details.
3. Select the product or service type.
4. Briefly describe your business and click Continue.
5. Submit a cover letter and relevant evidence.
6. Click Preview & Submit Dispute.

You can click Save Draft to finish later. Watch the deadline shown under the chargeback reason. Deadlines vary by card network (for example, 18 days for Visa and 40 days for Mastercard), and once it passes the chargeback is final. Wix doesn't decide the outcome; the banks and payment networks do.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/chargebacks-in-wix-payments

Updating Your Payment Details in Wix for Failed or Declined Renewal Payments
Troubleshooting Pending PayPal Payments
response:
A **Failed** payout means the money from Wix Payments didn't reach your bank account. The payout and any other funds that have finished processing are placed **On Hold** until the blocking issue is identified and resolved. Once it's fixed, the funds are included in your next scheduled payout.

Common causes include incorrect bank details or your bank changing ownership. To check the details:

1. Click the failed payout in your Wix Payments dashboard to see the specific issue and resolution instructions. You can also click **Payouts on Hold** for this information.
2. Go to **Accept Payments** in your site's dashboard and click **Manage** next to Wix Payments.
3. Click **Edit Account Details** next to Account Details, check the Bank Details, correct anything needed, and click **Resubmit**.

Also make sure the bank account holder's name matches the name on your Wix Payments account, and that your bank can receive EFT payments (ACH transfers if you're in the United States). If it can't, enter a different bank account in the same section and click **Resubmit**.

Source: https://support.wix.com/en/article/failed-payout-in-wix-payments

1. Open the **mobile editor**.
2. Scroll to the bottom of the page.
3. Click an area of the page body close to the footer.
4. Double-click the **Page Height** icon to remove the gaps between the page and footer.

If gaps appear between sections, try these:

- Use the **Spacing Guide** tool to see the gap sizes and spot which ones are uneven.
- Use the **Auto Space on Drag** tool when you drag elements to even out spacing.
- If an element is stretched to full width, zoom out to 50% and move elements up or down to close the gaps.

Keep in mind that changes made in the mobile editor don't affect your desktop site.
